CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md

What this is

zuspark is a Spark Connect client for R with no JVM, no Python and no Spark installation. It connects to an sc:// endpoint, runs SQL there and returns the result as Arrow, speaking the protocol itself: gRPC through zugrpc, protobuf through zuproto, Arrow IPC through zuarrow, ids from zuid. It is an application package, pure R over those four Imports. v0.1.0 covers SQL only: connect, run a statement, read a schema, collect or stream rows, interrupt, disconnect. It is deliberately not a DBI driver, a dplyr backend, a plan builder, a UDF runner, a local Spark or an ML or streaming client; the DBI shim and the rest are later versions.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0070. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides. Its decisions (§13) and open questions (§15) are recorded there, not here.

Current state

Stages 0 to 4 done 2026-11-05: the descriptor set pinned at Spark v4.2.1, and sessions: spark_connect(), spark_disconnect(), spark_config(), spark_version(), spark_session_id(), zuspark_info(), and SQL with reattachable execution: spark_sql(), spark_collect(), spark_fetch(), spark_execute() (Stage 2), and spark_schema() (Stage 3), and Spark’s errors, spark_error_details(), interrupts and spark_interrupt() (Stage 4). Stage 5, 2026-11-06: spark_connect_databricks(), checked on a Databricks Free Edition workspace (serverless only; classic clusters untested), with findings in .agents/databricks.md. Stage 6, 2026-11-06: the live suite covers §7 and §8, hostile responses are tested, and §10’s benchmarks are in .agents/benchmarks.md. Stage 7, 2026-11-06: the README, the reference index and the articles “Get started”, “Spark without the JVM” and “Connect to Databricks”. Stage 8 turned on nosuggests and nold; Stage 9 made it 0.1.0, a GitHub release with Remotes: (design Q6). Stage 10, 2026-11-07: the critical review’s 14 blocking and required findings fixed (#25 to #31, #39 to #45), and the CRAN review clean on 3838f65; v0.1.0 is at 100%. The review’s suggestions and questions (#32 to #38, #46 to #62) remain open for later versions. Exact conversion of int64, decimal128 and the time types is left out of 0.1.0 and waits on zuint, decimal and zutempo registering with zuarrow (zuint#52, decimal#24, zutempo#94). The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0. Release is gated on five siblings reaching CRAN (design §4). None is on CRAN yet; zugrpc (verified 2026-11-05 at ba9d83b) already works against live Spark on zuhttp’s and zuproto’s main, and its own release waits on zuhttp#40 and zuproto#13. Its R API can still change before then.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is the v0.1.0 issue, created by pkg-roadmap. Sibling packages that depend on this one before CRAN does: none.

Commands

The siblings come from GitHub until they reach CRAN, through Remotes:; pak::pak("pedrobtz/zugrpc") also pulls zuhttp and zuproto.

The live tests need a Spark Connect 4.2.1 server; without Docker, Podman runs the same image:

podman run -d --name spark -p 15002:15002 -e SPARK_NO_DAEMONIZE=true \
  docker.io/apache/spark:4.2.1 /opt/spark/sbin/start-connect-server.sh \
  --conf spark.connect.grpc.binding.address=0.0.0.0
ZUSPARK_TEST_REMOTE=sc://localhost:15002 Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'
Rscript tools/record-fixtures.R sc://localhost:15002   # re-record fixtures

The reattach test needs a second server that cuts streams, with a heap large enough to buffer range(10^8); the reattach fixture is recorded from one that cuts after 2 KB (tools/record-fixtures.R says how):

podman run -d --name spark-cut -p 15003:15002 -e SPARK_NO_DAEMONIZE=true \
  docker.io/apache/spark:4.2.1 /opt/spark/sbin/start-connect-server.sh \
  --driver-memory 3g --conf spark.connect.grpc.binding.address=0.0.0.0 \
  --conf spark.connect.execute.reattachable.senderMaxStreamDuration=1s \
  --conf spark.connect.execute.reattachable.senderMaxStreamSize=1m
ZUSPARK_TEST_REMOTE_CUT=sc://localhost:15003 \
  Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "live")'

The databricks fixture comes from a workspace instead, by tools/record-databricks.R with DATABRICKS_HOST and DATABRICKS_TOKEN set; it scrubs the workspace’s names and fails if one survives. Keep the credentials outside the repository (.zuspark-databricks.env is ignored in case a copy lands here).

The README and the articles run against a server: render the README with SPARK_REMOTE=sc://localhost:15002 Rscript -e 'devtools::build_readme()' and commit README.md; pkgdown.yaml starts Spark 4.2.1 and sets SPARK_REMOTE for the site, so a chunk that fails there fails the build. The Databricks article’s chunks never run (they need a workspace).

tools/run-benchmarks.R <remote> <python> measures design §10 against PySpark (tools/benchmarks.py, in a venv with pyspark-client==4.2.1 and pyarrow) and prints the table for .agents/benchmarks.md. The 10^7-row rows need a server with --driver-memory 3g; the default 1g runs out of heap.

Re-record the fixtures when a stage adds an RPC scenario or the request shape changes, and commit them with the change.

sh tools/build-descriptors.sh rebuilds inst/proto/spark-connect.binpb and inst/proto/VERSION (needs curl and protoc). It is occasional: run it only when a pin at its top changes, and commit the set, VERSION and NOTICE together; test-proto.R checks the hash.

Architecture

See .agents/design.md for the why; this is the where.

  • R/proto.R loads the shipped descriptor set into one zuproto pool per R session (spark_pool()).
  • R/transport.R: every RPC goes through spark_rpc(), which encodes, calls con$transport and decodes. The transport is bound when the connection is made: normally a unary zugrpc call, in tests the fake channel from the zuspark.transport option. The zuspark.record option writes each call’s bytes for the fixtures.
  • R/execute.R: execute_plan() runs one ExecutePlan with reattachable execution: the reattach loop, inline releases every 16 responses, release-all on completion or abandonment, and the per-response checks. R/sql.R builds the user verbs on it.
  • R/databricks.R: spark_connect_databricks(), the connection string and compute header Databricks needs.
  • R/url.R parses sc:// strings; R/session.R holds the connection, an environment of class zuspark_connection, so the server-side id and the released flag are shared by every copy; R/config.R is spark_config().
  • R/conditions.R: zuspark_abort() raises every zuspark_error, base R conditions only. R/errors.R turns zugrpc’s conditions into zuspark’s, in spark_rpc() and spark_stream(); R/interrupt.R handles Ctrl-C during a read and spark_interrupt().

Licences of the bundled protocol files are in inst/COPYRIGHTS.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • No src/ (D3). zuspark is pure R; native code lives in zuhttp and zuarrow. test-abi.R fails if a shared library is ever built or loaded.
  • The descriptor set is built by a tools/ script, never at install time (D4). It ships compiled in inst/proto/, pinned to the Spark tag of the live-test image with its SHA-256 recorded; the two are re-pinned together, and re-pinning re-runs the proto snapshots.
  • Every request goes through session_fields(), which carries the session id, user context and client type, and refuses a released connection; every response goes through observe_session(). A new RPC that skips either loses the session checks of design §7.2.
  • A new execution path goes through execute_plan(). It is what releases the server’s buffer; an ExecutePlan that bypasses it leaves the result in the server’s memory until the session dies.
  • The channel is never stored on the connection. It lives in the namespace’s channels registry, reached by connection_channel(con): its headers hold the bearer token, and connections travel inside queries and errors that users save or send to other processes (#26).
  • The transport is read from con$transport, never from the option at call time. A finalizer runs after the test that set the option has gone; binding at connect is what keeps it off the network.
  • zuspark’s error classes keep zugrpc’s after them. The reattach loop and release_session() match zugrpc_error_transport and zugrpc_error_unimplemented on conditions zuspark has already converted; dropping zugrpc’s classes would break both silently.
  • No type conversion of zuspark’s own (D10). Every row goes to zuarrow untouched, timestamps included; the R edge is zuarrow’s lossy rule.
  • No threads, no background work, no retries beyond reattach (D8, D13). One channel, one call at a time; a release that silently re-runs a statement with side effects is worse than an error.

Testing

The conformance oracle is PySpark and the live server: recorded request and response fixtures replayed through a fake channel on every leg, live Spark Connect in a container on the Ubuntu legs only (design §9), since only Ubuntu runners have Docker.

  • helper-fixtures.R: local_replay() replays a scenario of tests/testthat/fixtures/ in order, failing on a call out of order, and collects the decoded requests; responses overrides a recorded answer by call number (bytes, or a function that may signal), which is how version, session and status cases are made without recording them. replay_connect() connects with the scenario’s recorded session id, and mocks new_operation_id() so that each execution gets the operation id it was recorded with. Streaming calls replay message by message; edit_response() and which_response() rewrite one recorded message, and a condition in the message list is signalled when the stream reaches it.
  • helper-types.R: the type matrix, fixtures/types/types.csv, one query per Spark type, and PySpark’s Arrow bytes for each, recorded by tools/pyspark-types.py inside the Spark container (it needs pip install pyarrow pandas grpcio grpcio-status googleapis-common-protos zstandard there first). Re-record them with the fixtures when the Spark pin moves.
  • helper-live.R: test-live-*.R run only with ZUSPARK_TEST_REMOTE set, and the reattach test only with ZUSPARK_TEST_REMOTE_CUT, a server that cuts streams (see Commands); tools/ci-live-tests.R runs them in live.yaml and fails if one skips.
  • test-hostile.R replays sql-query with one response truncated, flipped or given oversized counts; a malformed message must be a zuspark_protocol_error, and any damage must end in a result or a zuspark_error. It takes about five seconds. The fixture suite takes about ten seconds; the live range(10^8) reattach test about a minute.

A gap found in zugrpc while testing is filed there as a zugrpc issue, not worked around here. Add the helpers and the suite’s runtime here as stages land. The conventions every package follows are in .claude/shared/r-package.md.

Continuous integration

R-CMD-check.yaml and coverage.yaml call the shared pedrobtz/r-actions workflows at @v1; pkgdown.yaml builds and deploys the site with r-lib/actions. live.yaml is this package’s own: it starts Spark Connect 4.2.1 in Docker on Ubuntu, plus a second server that cuts streams for the reattach test, and runs the live tests, because R CMD check never touches a network. Stage 2 is the first full stage; the stages marked full are listed in .agents/roadmap.md. What a change runs and what the CI labels do is in .claude/shared/ci.md.
